title: Applied AI Engineer
description: Konsert Strategy & IP is a leading consultancy at the intersection of business strategy, technology and intellectual property. Founded in Gothenburg in 2006, we work with some of the world's largest technology-intensive companies, close to the leaders who decide where to compete and how to win through technology and IP. Since 2024 we have been part of the international Rouse Group.Like every consultancy, we are adapting to an environment that AI is reshaping. Much of the research, analysis and preparation that used to fill a project team's weeks can now be done by machines.Our clients face the same shift from the other side. Their strategy, technology and IP functions are under a clear mandate to work faster and leaner with AI. But today's landscape of point tools depends on the user to supply the context, and without it the tools speed up the doing without improving the thinking.What clients still need is sound judgment, grounded in the right context. That is where the real value of AI lies: not in faster work, but in better, more reliable and more impactful decisions. So rather than defend the old consultancy model, we are rebuilding ours around that: consultants who work inside our clients' organizations, supported by an AI platform that holds the client's context. That platform is Sapivia. We are now growing our in-house tech team, to make sure we have the capabilities under our own roof to take Sapivia to the next level.What we are building: SapiviaSapivia is Konsert's AI platform. At its core is the context layer: a client-specific knowledge graph that holds the context every decision depends on. How the business, its technology and its intellectual property connect, what depends on what, and the reasoning behind the decisions already made. We have built that picture for clients by hand for twenty years; Sapivia captures it, keeps it alive and makes it available to people and AI alike.Our consultants build the context layer together with the client. The client's own people, Konsert's forward-deployed strategists and the AI tools the client already uses can then reason and act on the same picture, one that grows richer over time.Sapivia is already in use with clients, starting in IP, where the need is sharpest. But the same picture answers the questions every technology company has to ask: which technologies matter, where to compete and how to turn knowledge into advantage. That is where we are taking it next.The Konsert tech core teamWe are building a small tech core team: a handful of engineers with complementary skills. The team is led by a Tech Lead and sits in Gothenburg, next to the consultants who deploy Sapivia with clients. Build work happens in close collaboration with those consultants, several of whom spend part of their time in the team, so the domain expertise and the client's reality are in the room when we build.We work in an agile way with shared ownership: everyone is close to the users, effort goes where it is needed, and the team ships several times a week and owns the result together. Development runs in close alignment with Konsert's leadership team, with short paths to user input and quick decisions. The tech core team has a central voice in how Sapivia is shaped. Around this core, we scale with external developers and the Rouse Group's technology organization.Questions we are working on right nowGiving AI the right context is only the start. Turning that context into decisions that large companies can rely on raises questions that few teams have answered yet. These are some of the ones we are working on now. They are open questions, not tickets, and you will help answer them.How do we assure the quality of AI responses at scale, when the right answer is often a matter of judgment?How do we best combine deep domain knowledge with what the models already know?How do we make a rich, connected body of knowledge feel simple and intuitive to work with?How do we give large organizations precise control over who sees what, across regions, teams and many users?How do we shorten the path from prototype to production code, while keeping the freedom to experiment?The role: Applied AI engineerYou bring the applied AI competence to the core team. Sapivia's AI features run on the client-specific knowledge graph as their context layer, and the hard problems are in the harness around the models: retrieval, context management, tools, guardrails, evaluation and feedback loops. You take LLM-based features from first prompt to production, set up the evaluation that assures their quality, and help the team decide where AI creates value and where it does not. You work closely with the consultants whose judgment the system is meant to support.What You BringSeveral years (likely 5+) of professional experience as a software engineerExperience building and shipping LLM-based features in a real product, including prompt design and systematic evaluationExperience with retrieval over structured and unstructured data, ideally combining graph traversal with vector search and embeddingsExperience designing the harness around models: tool use, context management, guardrails and agent loops that run server-side with controlled budgetsComfort working in TypeScript or C#, the main languages of the platform; Python experience is welcomeExperience with Azure OpenAI or comparable hosted model services, and with data pipelines and data quality, is a plusA habit of using AI effectively in your own work, and of measuring rather than assumingWho we are looking forYou are an experienced engineer who has shipped software that real users depend on. Where you have worked matters less than what you have built. If you are more senior and want to shape a platform and a team from an early stage, we would like to talk to you too.Beyond that, we look for four things:You share ownership of the outcome. You care about what the team ships, not only your part of it, and you help get the work done where it is needed.You are curious about the domain and the users. You want to understand what a better decision looks like for the people we build for, and you like working with consultants as closely as with other engineers.You use AI seriously in your own work, and you understand that AI in a product is only valuable when it is reliable and well grounded. Evaluation and guardrails interest you as much as capability does.You like building. You take initiative, form a view and can explain it, and you are comfortable when the playbook is still being written.If most of this describes you, please get in touch. Nobody matches every line, and we would rather hear from you than have you rule yourself out.Why KonsertHelp shape the model. We are building a service and a technology business together. The platform you build is what our consultants deploy, and your engineering judgment will shape our methods, our product and what we offer next.See it in use. You will see your work in clients' real decisions and operations, and hear from the consultants next to you how it lands.Responsibility, with experience beside you. We are a team of around twenty with a flat structure. You will take on responsibility early, with a Tech Lead and senior colleagues to support you.A solid base. Konsert has an established position in technology strategy and business-driven IP, and Sapivia is already in use with clients. Since 2024 we have been part of the international Rouse Group, which gives us specialist expertise, technology resources and a wider client network. Show more Show less

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Evals
description: Who We AreYou've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.About The TeamJoin the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.About The RoleEvaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.What The Role InvolvesDesign evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.Minimum QualificationsAt least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.Preferred QualificationsExperience with language-model training or post-training.Experience with agent or gaming environments.Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.What We OfferOwnership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.Why Prosus?At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth.
